issues.message: Only 41 blocks: too bare for a common (at least 50). Carlton wants more detail, not less.
12 % detail blocks: on the bare side, aim for 20 %+.

notes.roof: solid two-layer wool block, not an awning

visual.summary: Spruce posts and a counter with barrels under a striped wool canopy. The canopy dominates and the colours clash.
problems: The canopy is two full layers of solid blue and light-blue wool, bigger and heavier than the stall under it: from every view the stall is a bright blue box. Make the awning one block thick (or wool on the front edge and carpet/trapdoors behind), sloping down to the front
Colours: the saturated blue/cyan clashes with the medieval palette of every other structure. Use red and white like the butcher's awning, or brown/white, yellow/white
The counter and goods sit deep under the canopy and are half hidden; push the goods to the front edge so they show
Prop, so 'too small' is a false alarm; but L1 has almost no goods

issues.message: 60 blocks, over the prop budget of 30 (docs/STRUCTURES.md). A warning only.

notes.roof: Still a little heavy: the back canopy is wool on a full plank layer (two blocks thick); a single layer would look lighter. Not blocking.

visual.summary: Spruce stall with a counter, barrels, crates and hay under a two-tier red and white awning. Now it looks like a market stall.
problems: Round 1 fixes are in: red and white stripes instead of neon blue, and the front awning is one layer stepping down from the back. Still a little heavy: the back canopy is wool on a full plank layer (two blocks thick); a single layer would look lighter. Not blocking.

issues.message: 62 blocks, over the prop budget of 30 (docs/STRUCTURES.md). A warning only.

notes.detail: Fine for the shell level: barrels, chest, hay on the counter, trade sign and the new flower pot (tulip comes from the decoration step); still on the plain side, as an L1 should be.
notes.roof: Earlier asks are done: the front awning is now one thin layer (top-half trapdoors with red/white carpet, y2-3, z1-2) and the back canopy is carpet on one plank layer instead of wool on planks, so it reads lighter. Stepped two-height canopy with a front overhang.
notes.materials: Red/white stripes (the colour fix from v2) on spruce logs and planks; the oak wall sign is the only odd wood, too small to matter.
notes.life: Only the flower pot; fine for L1, L2 and L3 add the rest.
notes.levels: L1 bare stall, L2 adds the striped valance, lanterns and produce, L3 the lamp post, banner and greenery: tell apart at a glance.

visual.summary: Level 1 is the stall shell: spruce posts, plank counter with a hay bale and trade sign at the front edge, a flower pot on the front-left barrel, a chest and barrel at the back under a thin two-step striped awning. The round 2 asks (goods at the counter edge, a flower pot) are done.
